column1: # Every upstream report this project has filed, one per line. This file is the
# record; spike/upstream-report-status.sh reads it rather than carrying a list
# of its own, and spike/check-upstream-ledger.sh holds it to the markers in
# docs/target-classes.md in both directions (#297).
# Before this file existed, the status script carried a hand-written literal and
# a report filed without editing that literal was invisible: the table looked
# whole, every row read fine, and the script exited 0. The cohort-4 close
# depended on remembering to add himalaya by hand (PR #253).
# Columns (tab-separated, exactly four, TABS not spaces):
#   owner/repo  number  status  finding
#   status   standing   the report stands on the tracker; the status script
#                       measures it
#            withdrawn  filed and then withdrawn. It is still something that was
#                       filed, so it belongs here - a withdrawn report and an
#                       unlisted one look identical on a tracker, and this column
#                       is what separates them
#   finding  the tool's name as docs/target-classes.md spells it in the second
#            column of its row. Not free text: the checker uses it to require
#            that the marker sits on that tool's row rather than merely
#            somewhere in the file
# All four of those are checked, and each was a way to lose a row quietly before
# it was: a row with three fields, or written with spaces, parsed to nothing and
# vanished from both scripts saying nothing; a status typo dropped a standing
# report and the table still printed "N of N"; a marker could sit on any row at
# all. The checker refuses on each rather than skipping the row.
# WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE: a report filed without being written here AND without a
# marker in docs/target-classes.md. Prose in that file naming a filing is not
# enough - only a marker is. The check holds these two records to each other;
# nothing in it reaches a tracker. That gap is named rather than closed.
